title: Data Mining
text: An introduction to discovering useful patterns and knowledge from large datasets. The course covers the data-mining process, classification, clustering, association rules, and their application to real-world data.

title: Data Mining
text:
Topics

Data Mining Overview — the KDD process and data preprocessing.
Classification — decision trees, Naive Bayes, KNN, and ensemble methods.
Clustering — partitional (K-means) and hierarchical (agglomerative) methods.
Association Rules — frequent itemsets and Apriori.
Evaluation & Interpretation — measuring and interpreting mining results.
Applications — segmentation, anomaly detection, and market analysis.

title: Data Mining
text:
Learning Outcomes
By the end of the course, students will be able to:

Apply the end-to-end data-mining process to a dataset.
Choose appropriate algorithms for classification, clustering, and association tasks.
Interpret and communicate discovered patterns.
Appreciate the ethical and privacy considerations of data mining.

Intelligent Agents — agent architectures, environments, and rationality.
Problem Solving & Search — uninformed and informed search, heuristics, and constraint satisfaction.
Knowledge Representation & Reasoning — logic, rules, and expert systems.

Machine Learning Foundations — supervised and unsupervised learning, model evaluation.
AI Applications — computer vision, NLP, and intelligent systems in practice.

title: Pattern Recognition
text: An introduction to recognizing patterns in data — with a strong emphasis on computer vision and machine-learning approaches used in real recognition systems.

title: Pattern Recognition
text:
Topics

Pattern Recognition Fundamentals — the recognition pipeline and feature extraction.
Feature Engineering — descriptors, feature matching, and representation.
Classical Classifiers — nearest neighbors, Bayes, and support vector machines.
Deep Learning for Recognition — CNNs, transfer learning, and modern architectures.
Computer Vision Applications — document analysis, object detection, and image classification.
Evaluation — accuracy, precision/recall, and real-world constraints.

title: Pattern Recognition
text:
Learning Outcomes
By the end of the course, students will be able to:

Design a recognition pipeline from raw data to classification.
Select and apply feature-based and deep-learning methods appropriately.
Evaluate recognition systems with appropriate metrics.
Understand the trade-offs between classical and deep approaches.

I am a lecturer (Asisten Ahli) in the Department of Electrical Engineering at the Faculty of Science and Technology, Universitas Jambi. title: About
text:
I am Akhiyar Waladi, a lecturer (Asisten Ahli) in the Department of Electrical Engineering, Faculty of Science and Technology, Universitas Jambi, where I teach and research topics in artificial intelligence, machine learning, pattern recognition, and predictive systems.
My path into computing started at IPB University (Institut Pertanian Bogor), where I earned my Bachelor of Computer Science in 2017. During my undergraduate years I explored embedded systems and computer vision — co-developing an Automated Fish Counter, an embedded system integrated with an Android device for automated fish measurement, counting, and sorting (showcased on Devpost). I continued to a Master of Computer Science at Universitas Indonesia (2018–2020), where I deepened my work on pattern recognition and machine learning, including research on automatic counting of scanned election forms using feature matching and convolutional neural networks.
Between 2018 and 2024 I worked in industry as a Data Scientist, first at kumparan (2018–2020) in Jakarta and then at Alfagift – Global Loyalty Indonesia (2020–2024) in Tangerang. In these roles I built and maintained data products, forecasting systems, recommendation and segmentation models, and end-to-end machine-learning pipelines used by millions of retail customers.
Since September 2024, I have been a lecturer at Universitas Jambi. I currently teach undergraduate courses in the electrical engineering program, supervise student projects, and lead community-service (pengabdian) programs that bring AI and IoT literacy to schools, pesantren, and vocational students in the Jambi region.

title: Research
text: My research applies artificial intelligence, machine learning, and pattern recognition to solve practical problems in agriculture, health, industry, and public administration. I work primarily with deep learning, computer vision, time-series forecasting, and clustering methods.

title: Research
text:
Research Themes

Pattern Recognition & Computer Vision
I develop recognition systems for structured and unstructured visual data — from scanned election forms and remote sensing scenes to agricultural and medical imagery.

Automatic counting based on scanned election form using feature match and CNN — a system that automatically tallies votes from scanned election forms (ICACSIS 2019, Scopus-indexed).
Transfer learning for remote sensing scene classification — benchmarking CNN and Vision Transformer architectures for scene recognition.
Multi-architecture CNN analysis for automated malaria detection — detecting Plasmodium species and lifecycle stages in microscopy images with YOLO and CNN variants.
Land cover classification — improving accuracy of Sentinel-2 land cover classification using Random Forest.
Automated Fish Counter — embedded vision system for fish measurement, counting, and sorting.



Predictive Systems & Time-Series Forecasting
I build forecasting and prediction models for economic, energy, and market data.

Prediksi Nilai Ekspor Migas Indonesia — forecasting Indonesian oil & gas export values using SARIMA and LSTM (SATESI, 2025).
Stock price prediction with LSTM — machine-learning approach to stock price forecasting (Media JISI, 2025).
Predictive analytics for education trends — KNN-based analysis of Indonesian education data 2021–2023.
Predictive systems are a core expertise area: designing and building computational systems that turn historical data into actionable forecasts.



Machine Learning, Clustering & Segmentation
I use unsupervised and supervised learning to reveal structure in data.

K-means customer segmentation — clustering for effective marketing strategy (Media JISI, 2025).
Hierarchical clustering of Indonesian provinces — grouping provinces by household gas usage ratio (JEKIN, 2025).
Hotspot clustering in Bangka Belitung Islands — agglomerative hierarchical clustering for fire hotspot analysis.
Instagram engagement analysis — machine-learning classification of visual and temporal features.



Expert Systems & Intelligent Computing
I design domain-specific decision-support and intelligent systems, an area I teach and apply through community-service projects:

Rancang bangun sistem komputasi — construction of computational systems for real users.
IoT monitoring systems — smart farming plant monitoring taught to vocational (SMK) students.
Financial information systems — data-management systems for pesantren administrators.
